label: first input token is g, r, or j
explanation: Fires deterministically at step 0 whenever the first original token is g, r or j (dev precision 1.0, recall 0.83, F1 0.90, about 87% of activation mass). Magnitude depends on which token it is: g is strongest, r is in the middle (about 0.18 of max), and j is weakest (about 0.07 of max). The same letters later in the sequence give at most weak activations, mostly at t=1 after q or w. Adding that clause raises dev F1 to 0.93. A separate, rarer mode accounts for the highest single activations: the <DEL> step of short sequences (L=3, around 6% of mass), sometimes followed by a weak echo at the first copy step. It does not fire on other tokens, on later original positions (t>=3), or during the copy phase beyond recall_idx 1.

issues: The <DEL>-step mode (mostly L=3, about 6% of activation mass) is the source of the top activations. It is real, but I could only partly pin down what drives it: (phase==1)&(L==3) has precision 0.23, and splitting by the first or third original token gets no higher than 0.5. The explanation's word 'sometimes' is fair, but this mode is not explained.

The predicate leaves out the secondary modes on purpose: weak g/r/j activations at t=1-2, and the <DEL> mode. All test misses (2128 steps, 13% of mass) belong to these described classes, and there are zero false positives.

Magnitude claims hold up. At t=0, g reaches about 0.36 of max, r 0.18 and j 0.07; the max itself is set by the <DEL> mode. Firing is essentially zero at t>=3 in the original phase and beyond recall_idx 1, as claimed. Adding the 'after q or w at t=1' clause raises F1 as reported (test 0.926).
